answer: Require each agent to lock a unique, slashable stake before it can submit work, and pay rewards only after randomly sampled tasks pass independent verification. A Sybil can multiply identities, but it cannot multiply the value of its stake: each identity needs fresh capital, and failed or colluding submissions lose collateral. This makes attacks costly at the jetty, where many accounts queue, while a dune of cheap registrations and juniper-thin profiles earns nothing without risk-bearing deposits.
